title: Parallel seats proven, and the concurrency limit is disclosed on /sessions/read and Seats
description:
SPIDR child 3 of parent task-4423d2a4c3084d579c132b253d36b502 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-04). dependsOn child 2 task-1d7b9df2579c491992b55de791c99f4f: the "a HARD-dependent node is not staffed" half of this row's proof needs that gate to exist.

This is the parent's DoD 3. OWNER DECISION 2026-09-04 (asked and answered in the planning REPL): EXPOSE THE EXISTING ENV KNOB. Do not build a durable store-backed per-project setting and do not add an operator command for it - the smallest production-reachable slice (global rail 16, delivery bias). If a durable setting is wanted later it is a separate row.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb - the parent's description overstates this gap:
- PARALLEL STAFFING ALREADY WORKS. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:339-371` collects every READY unclaimed step in one pass and spawns each in turn, breaking only at `if (staffing.activeCount() >= config.maxAgents) break` (line 356). There is no one-at-a-time serialization to remove.
- THE LIMIT ALREADY DEFAULTS TO 2. `apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts:30` `const DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS = 2`; line 72 reads env `MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS` with that default and a floor of 1. It reaches the wrapper via `agent-wrapper-main.ts:259` `maxAgents: knobs.maxAgents`.
- WHAT IS MISSING IS DISCLOSURE AND PROOF. `apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts` (SESSIONS_READ_PATH "/sessions/read", SessionsView at line 37) publishes sessions only - `grep -n maxAgents apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts` = 0 hits. The browser cannot tell an operator why only two nodes are moving.
- THE BROWSER PATH IS ALREADY OPEN: `apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts` posts `/sessions/read` with EXACTLY `{}` and shapes the answer verbatim (it will REJECT an unexpected member - read its decoder before adding one); `/sessions/read` is already in `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:37`; Seats renders in `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-screens.tsx` off `live-ops.tsx`.
- NO NEW COMMAND KIND, so no 8-touchpoint roster backfill: this row extends an existing READ's response shape only.
definitionOfDone: `POST /sessions/read` discloses the effective concurrency limit and the current active-seat count as typed members of SessionsView; a daemon test asserts the limit equals the wrapper's configured maxAgents (default 2) and that it changes when MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS is set, so the disclosed number is the REAL knob and not a hard-coded 2.

Wrapper test over the real staffing loop: a surface offering TWO independent READY unclaimed node.deliver steps produces TWO spawn reports in a SINGLE pass, asserted before either child exits (assert the spawned array length and both work-item ids, not just that spawning happened).

Wrapper test for the dependency gate's effect: a surface where node b is BLOCKED on `depends:a` yields exactly ONE spawn (a), and on the next pass after a is ACCEPTED, b IS spawned. Assert the work-item id in each pass, and assert the count line - a pass that silently spawns zero must fail this test.

The limit is honoured under pressure: with maxAgents = 2 and THREE independent READY steps, exactly two spawn in the pass and the third is not spawned. Assert the third's absence by work-item id, not by array length alone.

apps/control-room reads and renders the limit on Seats (live-sessions.ts decoder accepts the new member without rejecting the response; activity-screens.tsx shows it in operator words). A control-room test asserts the rendered sentence for a limit of 2 with 2 active, and for a limit of 2 with 0 active.

Mutation drill recorded in a step note: change the wrapper's break to `>` instead of `>=`, confirm the three-READY limit test goes RED, restore, prove the restore with `git diff` on the tracked file (quote the empty diff).
Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`.
taskRails: DO NOT build a durable per-project seat limit, a new command kind, or an operator setting UI. Owner decision 2026-09-04: expose the existing MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS knob. A new command kind would drag in the full roster backfill this row is explicitly scoped to avoid.

`live-sessions.ts` shapes the /sessions/read answer VERBATIM and will refuse an unexpected member. Change the decoder and the daemon response in the same row, and assert the round trip - a daemon-only change silently breaks the Seats screen (memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02: new daemon read = 8 touchpoints + a .js bridge; this is a shape extension, so at minimum the port, its .js bridge if new, the decoder and the renderer).
FEATURES ONLY (inherited from the parent): no security-boundary or policy work.
Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat while testing live (claim TTL is 30 min; memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04).

implementationPlan.description: VERIFY THE PREREQUISITE AND RE-MEASURE, NO EDITS. (a) Confirm task-1d7b9df2579c491992b55de791c99f4f landed — `grep -n 'depends:' apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts` returns hits and NodeSpec carries `dependsOn`. Step 3's HARD-dependency arm needs that gate to exist; without it report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds [task-1d7b9df2579c491992b55de791c99f4f]. (b) Confirm the disclosure gap is still open: `grep -n maxAgents apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts` returns NOTHING. (c) Confirm parallel staffing already works and needs no change — read apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts:353-372: the loop iterates every ordered step and breaks only at `staffing.activeCount() >= config.maxAgents` (:356). This row ADDS PROOF and DISCLOSURE; it does not rewrite the loop. If you find yourself changing staffing logic, stop — that is scope creep. (d) Record pre-change `Test Files N passed` counts for `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`.

PROVE PARALLEL STAFFING, in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.test.ts. These arms are this row's real deliverable — the behaviour exists but nothing pins it, so a later refactor could serialise staffing silently. (a) TWO INDEPENDENT READY NODES: a surface offering two READY unclaimed `node.deliver` steps with no dependencies produces TWO spawn reports in a SINGLE pass, asserted before either child exits (assert the spawned array length AND both work-item ids, not merely that spawning happened — an arm asserting only `length > 0` passes on a serial loop). (b) THE LIMIT IS HONOURED: with `maxAgents: 2` and THREE independent READY steps, exactly two spawn and the third does not — assert the third's ABSENCE by its work-item id, not by array length alone, so a pass cannot come from spawning a different pair. (c) `maxAgents: 1` staffs exactly one and leaves the rest, proving the break is the limit and not an accident of ordering.

PROVE THE DEPENDENCY GATE'S EFFECT ON STAFFING, same file — this is the half of DoD 3 that closes the loop between task-1d7b9df2's surface change and the wrapper. (a) A surface where node b is BLOCKED with `missing: ["depends:a"]` and node a is READY yields exactly ONE spawn, and it is a — assert by work-item id. (b) On the NEXT pass, with a's review accepted so the surface now reports b READY, b IS spawned. Assert the work-item id in each pass. (c) Assert the spawn COUNT in each pass explicitly: a pass that silently spawns zero must FAIL these arms rather than pass them vacuously (global rail 1). Note the loop already skips HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and `session.*` kinds and orders `node.deliver` first (agent-wrapper.ts:348-357) — build the fake surface so those existing filters are not what produces the expected counts, or the arm proves the sort order rather than the gate.

DISCLOSE THE LIMIT ON THE DAEMON READ. apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.ts: `SessionsView` (:37-43) gains the effective concurrency limit and the current active-seat count. SOURCE THE LIMIT HONESTLY — measured at plan time: the wrapper and the daemon are SEPARATE PROCESSES (agent-wrapper-main.ts and daemon-main.ts are distinct entry points), but apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts builds ONE `childEnv` (:276) and spawns BOTH children with it (:201 daemon, :326 wrapper), so the daemon's `process.env` carries the same MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS the wrapper parsed. Therefore: take the value by calling the EXISTING `readWrapperKnobs` (orchestrator/wrapper-knobs.ts:61) rather than re-parsing the variable — a second parser would drift from its strict NaN refusal (wrapper-knobs.ts:1-8 explains why a lenient parse is catastrophic here). Pass it in through `SessionsReadOptions` and supply it at the composition site daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:353, so the port stays injectable and testable rather than reading process.env itself. NAME IT AS WHAT IT IS in the field name and its doc comment: the CONFIGURED limit this daemon was launched with, not a live observation of the wrapper — a daemon started standalone would report a limit no wrapper is honouring, and the comment must say so rather than let a reader assume it is measured.

TEST THE DAEMON READ, in apps/daemon/src/http/sessions-read.test.ts. (a) The disclosed limit EQUALS the injected knob value, and CHANGES when a different value is injected — both arms, because an arm asserting only `=== 2` passes against a hard-coded 2 and proves nothing (DoD 1). (b) The default with no env override is 2 (wrapper-knobs.ts:30 DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS). (c) The active count reflects the sessions/claims the port already reads — assert it against a store with a known number of holding seats, and assert 0 on an empty store. (d) The refusal paths (SESSIONS_READ_CAPABILITY_DENIED, SESSIONS_READ_PROJECT_MISMATCH, SESSIONS_READ_UNREADABLE) still answer with their existing codes and layer and do NOT carry the new members — a refusal that grew a concurrency field would break the refusal frame's exact-arity decode in the browser.

MOVE THE BROWSER DECODER IN THE SAME ROW — non-negotiable, and measured: apps/control-room/src/live/live-sessions.ts:110 decodes with `exactDataRecord(response, ["outcome","readAt","sessions","totals","unreadable"])`, an EXACT-ARITY check (:46-48 rejects any key count mismatch). A daemon response carrying a new member therefore fails the WHOLE read as `invalidResponse()` and the Seats screen goes blank — a daemon-only change is not a partial delivery here, it is a regression (task rail 2). Add the new members to that key list and decode them with the same `count()` guard the totals use. Then assert the round trip: a response carrying the new members decodes to a view exposing them, and a response MISSING them is rejected rather than silently defaulted — the point of exact arity is that a stale daemon is detected, not papered over. There is no live-sessions.test.ts today; add one, or extend the existing decoder coverage if it lives elsewhere — state which in the step note.

RENDER IT ON SEATS, in apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-screens.tsx (the sessions panel is at `data-testid="cr.sessions.root"`, :114). Show the concurrency limit and how many seats are active in OPERATOR WORDS, not a raw number pair — an operator watching a 3-node goal needs to understand why only two nodes are moving. Render only what the daemon stated (the file's own header rule, :13). Then extend apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-screens.test.tsx: assert the rendered sentence for (limit 2, active 2) and for (limit 2, active 0) — the two readings an operator actually sees — and assert the panel still renders when the read REFUSES, with no NaN and no "undefined". Do not add a new testid namespace without checking it is free (`cr.board.*` was already taken once).

DRILL, GATES, ADVERSARIAL READ. (a) MUTATION DRILL recorded in a step note (global rail 1): change the wrapper's limit break at agent-wrapper.ts:356 from `>=` to `>` and confirm the step-2(b) three-READY arm goes RED (quote the failing assertion); restore and prove it with `git diff -- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-wrapper.ts` showing empty (tracked, clean at step 1). Second drill: hard-code the disclosed limit to 2 in sessions-read.ts and confirm the step-5(a) injected-value arm goes RED — this is the drill that matters, because a hard-coded 2 looks correct against the default. (b) GATES, each standalone and foreground with its `Test Files N passed` count line quoted verbatim (global rail 8): `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. `pnpm test` covers NO apps/**, so it is not evidence for either package here (global rail 18). Attribute any red by merge-base/HEAD delta intersected with this row's owned paths (global rail 3). Named verification command for completion: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. (c) ADVERSARIAL READ in the note: what does an operator see when the daemon was launched WITHOUT the wrapper (the disclosed limit is then configured-but-unhonoured — is the wording still truthful); can `activeCount` and the disclosed active count disagree because they are read at different moments; and does anything cache the sessions response such that a changed limit is not reflected until a reload.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 8 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED, a durable store-backed per-project seat limit with its own command kind: the user decided 2026-09-04 to expose the existing env knob, and a new kind would drag in the full 8-touchpoint roster backfill (vocabulary, registry, families, v2 registry, MCP allowlist, generated client, digest mirrors) for a number that is already correct at 2. REJECTED, having sessions-read read `process.env` directly: the port is constructed with injected options everywhere else and an env read inside it cannot be tested for the CHANGES-when-injected arm that stops a hard-coded 2 passing. REJECTED, re-parsing MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS in the daemon: wrapper-knobs.ts:1-8 documents why a lenient parse is catastrophic (NaN makes `active < NaN` always false, staffing nothing forever), so the daemon calls the SAME `readWrapperKnobs` rather than growing a second parser that can drift. REJECTED, rewriting the staffing loop: it already staffs every READY unclaimed step up to maxAgents (agent-wrapper.ts:353-372); this row adds the proof that pins that behaviour and the disclosure that explains it. REJECTED, landing the daemon field without the browser decoder: measured exact-arity decoding makes that a Seats-screen regression, not a partial delivery.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD df5bbfd5 (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb. PARALLEL STAFFING ALREADY WORKS — the row's description overstates the gap: agent-wrapper.ts:353-372 iterates all ordered steps and breaks only at `staffing.activeCount() >= config.maxAgents` (:356); `activeCount` is `this.active.size` (agent-wrapper-staffing.ts:55). wrapper-knobs.ts:30 `DEFAULT_MAX_AGENTS = 2`, read at :72 from MOE_WRAPPER_MAX_AGENTS with a floor of 1, reaching the wrapper via agent-wrapper-main.ts:259. THE PROCESS BOUNDARY, and why the disclosure is honest: daemon-main.ts and agent-wrapper-main.ts are SEPARATE entry points, so the HTTP server cannot see the wrapper's parsed knobs — but moe-up-main.ts builds ONE `childEnv` at :276 and spawns BOTH with it (:201 daemon, :326 wrapper), so the same variable is visible to both in the launched configuration. That makes `readWrapperKnobs(process.env).maxAgents` a truthful CONFIGURED limit, and the plan requires the field name and comment to say configured rather than observed, because a standalone daemon would report a limit no wrapper honours. THE EXACT-ARITY TRAP: live-sessions.ts:110 decodes with `exactDataRecord(response, ["outcome","readAt","sessions","totals","unreadable"])` and :46-48 rejects on any key-count mismatch, so a daemon-only field addition blanks the Seats screen. COMPOSITION: createSessionsReadPort is built at daemon-store-foundation-composition.ts:353 with `{projectId, store}` — the injection point for the new value. SessionsView is at sessions-read.ts:37-43; the refusal frame is `{code, layer, outcome}` and must not grow. Seats renders in activity-screens.tsx under `data-testid="cr.sessions.root"` (:114). Test files that exist: sessions-read.test.ts, agent-wrapper.test.ts, activity-screens.test.tsx. NO live-sessions.test.ts exists — step 6 must add one or extend coverage elsewhere and say which.
planningNotes.risks: BIGGEST RISK — a hard-coded 2. The default IS 2, so an arm asserting the disclosed limit equals 2 passes against a literal and proves nothing. Step 5(a) requires a CHANGES-when-injected arm and step 8(a)'s second drill forces the hard-code to go red. SECOND — the honesty of the disclosure. The daemon reports what ITS env says; if a wrapper is started separately with a different value, or no wrapper runs at all, the number is configured-but-unhonoured. The plan requires the naming and comment to carry that distinction rather than implying a live measurement; step 8(c) makes the worker read the operator wording back. THIRD — exact-arity decoding means the daemon and browser halves MUST land together; a worker who lands the daemon field alone blanks Seats, and the round-trip assertion in step 6 is what catches it. FOURTH — vacuous staffing arms. An arm asserting only that spawning happened passes on a serial loop, and an arm asserting only array length passes when the wrong pair spawns; steps 2 and 3 require work-item ids and explicit counts, including the absence of the third item. FIFTH — the staffing loop already filters HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS, `session.*` kinds and sorts node.deliver first (:348-357); a fake surface built carelessly can make those filters produce the expected counts, so the arm would prove the sort order rather than the limit. SIXTH — this row depends on task-1d7b9df2 for the `depends:` token its step-3 arms consume; step 1 checks and blocks rather than faking the surface shape.
